body:
Walk into any vape shop or browse any online catalog and you will see two kinds of nicotine on the label of e-liquid: salts and freebase. They look similar on the shelf, but they behave differently in your device, they come in different strengths and they suit different hardware. Choosing the wrong one for your setup is one of the most common reasons a new vaper finds the experience harsh, leaky or disappointing. This guide explains what each type is, how they feel, which devices suit them, how they compare on cost and how to choose. It is general information for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## What freebase nicotine is
Freebase is the form of nicotine used in e-liquid for most of vaping's history. In freebase, nicotine is in its pure, unbound form, and it vaporizes easily. The trade-off is that it feels sharp on the throat, especially as strength rises. For that reason freebase liquids are made at lower strengths, commonly 0 to 12 mg/mL and occasionally up to about 24 mg/mL, and they are designed for devices that produce larger volumes of vapor per puff.

That sharper feel is called throat hit, and some people like it because it resembles the sensation of a traditional cigarette. Others find it unpleasant. If throat hit matters to you, our guide to [throat hit explained](/blog/throat-hit-explained/) covers what drives it.

## What nicotine salts are
Nicotine salts, usually written "nic salts", combine nicotine with an acid such as benzoic acid. This lowers the pH of the liquid, which makes the vapor feel smoother even at high strengths. The nicotine is also absorbed in a way that many users describe as quicker and more satisfying with fewer, smaller puffs. Because of the smoother feel, salts are sold at higher strengths, from around 20 mg/mL up to 50 mg/mL (5%), and they dominate pods and disposables.

Nearly every disposable vape on the market uses nicotine salts, which is why you will see 50mg (5%) so often on product pages. See the [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/) for how that number relates to what you vape.

## Side-by-side comparison
- **Typical strength:** freebase 0 to 12 mg/mL (sometimes higher); salts 20 to 50 mg/mL.
- **Feel at the throat:** freebase is sharper; salts are smoother.
- **Puff size:** freebase suits large puffs and big clouds; salts suit small, frequent puffs.
- **Best hardware:** freebase in higher-wattage and sub-ohm tanks; salts in low-power pods and small devices.
- **Bottle sizes:** freebase is often sold in 60 mL to 120 mL bottles; salts in 30 mL bottles.
- **PG/VG:** freebase often higher VG for clouds; salts often balanced or higher PG for pods. See [PG and VG ratios explained](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/).

## Which device suits which liquid
The device decides the answer more than preference does.

### Freebase devices
Sub-ohm tanks, rebuildable atomizers and many box mods use low-resistance coils that run at higher power and vaporize a lot of liquid per puff. A low-strength freebase liquid in a thicker, higher-VG blend works well here. The large puffs deliver plenty of nicotine even at 3 mg/mL.

### Salt devices
Pod systems, pen-style devices and disposables run at lower power with higher-resistance coils, which vaporize little liquid per puff. High-strength salts make up for the small puffs and stay smooth. Using a low-strength freebase in these devices can feel weak, and using salts in a powerful tank would be harsh.

If you are not sure what your device is, check the manual or the product page. Our [guide to disposable vs pod vs box mod](/blog/disposable-vs-pod-vs-box-mod/) explains the main categories.

## Cost and how long a bottle lasts
Because salts are used in small, frequent puffs at high strength, a 30 mL bottle can last a long time, and many people find salts economical for that reason. Freebase is typically bought in larger bottles because tanks use more liquid, and the cost per milliliter is often lower even though you use more of it. Compare cost per milliliter and the volume you expect to use per day, not just the price on the front. Our [bottle sizes guide](/blog/e-liquid-bottle-sizes-30ml-60ml-100ml/) explains what 30 mL, 60 mL and 100 mL mean in practice.

## Flavor and the two types
Both types can carry excellent flavor, and many brands release the same flavor in both formats. Salts tend to taste a touch smoother and sweeter because of the lower pH, while freebase can taste slightly more distinct and crisp. If you love a flavor in one format and want to try it in the other, expect it to be recognizable but not identical. You can browse both in our [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) range, where each product page lists its strength and bottle size.

## Mixing types and switching between them
Do not mix salts and freebase in the same bottle or tank, and avoid topping up one type into a tank still holding the other. Strength and pH will be unpredictable. When you switch, empty the tank, rinse it, replace the coil and start fresh. If you are going from freebase to salts, keep in mind that the jump in strength is large and your device must be designed for it, which means a pod system or similar. Take it gently, because the concentration is much higher than you are used to.

## Common mistakes
- **Using salts in a sub-ohm tank.** Concentration and puff size together are far too much.
- **Using low-strength freebase in a small pod.** It can feel weak and encourage frequent puffing.
- **Ignoring the PG/VG ratio.** A thick liquid in a small pod can fail to wick and burn the coil. See [why a vape tastes burnt](/blog/vape-tastes-burnt/).
- **Chasing strength.** A higher figure is not a better product.
- **Skipping the label.** Always confirm strength, volume and the hardware recommendation. Our guide to [reading an e-liquid label](/blog/how-to-read-an-e-liquid-label/) shows what to look for.

## How to choose, step by step
1. Identify your device type and its recommended power range.
2. Choose the nicotine type that matches: salts for low-power pods, freebase for tanks.
3. Pick a strength inside the normal range for that type, starting lower if you are unsure.
4. Choose a PG/VG ratio recommended for your hardware.
5. Choose a bottle size that fits how quickly you use liquid.
6. Pick a flavor you enjoy and plan to vape consistently, then judge it over several uses.

## Safety, storage and responsibility
Nicotine is addictive, and e-liquid is for adults aged 21 and over only. Keep bottles capped and out of reach of children and pets, store them in a cool, dark place and wipe up spills promptly. Our guide to [how to store e-liquid](/blog/how-to-store-e-liquid/) covers shelf life and storage in detail. If you have a medical condition or are pregnant or nursing, speak to a healthcare professional before using any nicotine product. Nothing here is medical advice.

## A practical way to test the difference
If you own both a pod device and a tank, the clearest way to understand the difference is to try a sensible product in each. Choose a nicotine-salt liquid at a moderate strength for the pod and a low-strength freebase for the tank, vape each for a few days and notice how many puffs you take, how the throat feels and how satisfied you are afterwards. Keep notes if that helps. Most people discover quickly which pairing matches their habits, and it is far cheaper to learn that with one bottle than with several.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Are salts stronger than freebase?
Salts are sold at higher listed strengths, but strength alone does not tell you how strong the experience is. Because salts are smoother, you can use them at 50 mg/mL in a small pod without the harshness that the same concentration of freebase would cause. The device, puff size and your habits matter as much as the label.

### Why do disposables use salts?
Disposables are small, low-power devices that vaporize a little liquid per puff. High-strength salts suit that design: they stay smooth at high concentration and deliver satisfaction in small, frequent puffs. A freebase liquid at the same concentration would be harsh in the same device.

### Do salts and freebase taste different?
Often slightly. The lower pH of salts can make flavor feel rounder and sweeter, while freebase can feel crisper. Makers adjust recipes for each type, so the same named flavor will be close but not identical.

### Which should a beginner choose?
Choose by device. If you are starting with a small pod kit or a disposable, salts are what the device is made for. If you are starting with a tank, begin with a low-strength freebase. Beginners get into trouble when they combine the wrong type with the wrong device, so match first and refine later.

### Can salts leak or gunk up a device faster?
Not because of the nicotine type itself. Leaks and gunk usually come from a mismatched ratio, overfilling or a worn coil. See [vape leaking causes and fixes](/blog/vape-leaking-causes-and-fixes/) and [how to clean a vape device](/blog/how-to-clean-a-vape-device/).

### Does the type change how I store the liquid?
No. Both are best kept capped, in a cool, dark place, away from heat and sunlight, and out of reach of children and pets. Check the date on the bottle and use older bottles first.

faq.q: What is the difference between nicotine salts and freebase?
faq.a: Freebase is nicotine in its pure form, which feels sharper and is sold at lower strengths. Salts bind nicotine to an acid, which feels smoother at higher strengths, so they are sold from about 20 to 50 mg/mL.

faq.q: Which type do disposable vapes use?
faq.a: Almost all disposable vapes use nicotine salts, typically listed as 50mg (5%).

faq.q: Can I use salts in my sub-ohm tank?
faq.a: It is not recommended. Salts are made for low-power pods, and in a powerful tank the concentration and puff size make the vapor harsh.
Often the cost per milliliter is lower for freebase because it is sold in larger bottles, but you also use more liquid. Compare cost per milliliter and your daily use.

faq.q: Can I mix salts and freebase?
faq.a: No. Mixing changes the strength and pH unpredictably. Empty and rinse the tank before switching types.

faq.q: How do I know which one my device needs?
faq.a: Check the manual or product page. Low-power pods and disposables suit salts; sub-ohm tanks and box mods suit freebase.
